note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording, the corpus-mined Old Testament verses and the translator-rendered Song of Songs the first edition carried.

Taylor sets the Song out line by line; each line now carries the OWB words that fall to it, split at OWB's own clause breaks, and a recurring verse is the same wherever it returns (2:3, 2:10/2:13, 2:17, 4:7, 5:2). Taylor's bracketed glosses ('(but)', '(the citron)', '(love-gifts)', '(or rather brilliant)', '(ardent love)', '(separation)') stay inside their lines; those lines are self_rendered. His quoted epithets follow OWB too: 'fairest among women' ከሴቶች ሁሉ ይልቅ ውብ የሆንሽ, 'Shulamite' ሱላማዊት, 'Prince's daughter' የመኳንንት ልጅ. Where his prose recites a line it follows OWB ('until the day breathe', 'among the lilies' በሱሰን አበቦች መካከል, 'mountains of spices' የቅመም ተራሮች, 'many waters'). Ecclesiastes 1:2 is OWB's 'breath' with a one-time gloss (ማለትም ከንቱ…), as other Amharic works have it. Joined OWB pieces use '…'.

`self_rendered` rows carry a `why`. Six places where OWB's Song reads differently from the text Taylor argues from are kept in the translator's wording and flagged as founder calls: 1:9 'a company of horses' (OWB 'a mare'), 3:6 'who is this' (OWB 'who is she'), the 2:7/3:5/8:4 refrain's 'My love … until she please' (OWB 'love … until it desires'), 6:12 'my willing people' (OWB 'Amminadib'), 8:5b's speaker, and 8:6 'a very flame of the LORD' (OWB 'a mighty flame').
